meta.title: Toward a neurospheroid niche model: optimizing embedded 3D bioprinting for fabrication of neurospheroid brain-like co-culture constructs.

extracted_by: Claude (Claude Code session), pending human review
summary: Neural spheroids were printed inside a soft GelMA support bath laden with astrocytes to build brain-like co-culture constructs. The 5% GelMA bath matched brain stiffness (~0.7 kPa) while allowing embedded printing.

formulations.stiffness_note: compressive modulus of 5 wt% GelMA bath after UV
formulations.review_notes: Species/source of the spheroid cells not captured; check the methods.
formulations.name: GelMA/gelatin/alginate ink in astrocyte-laden 5% GelMA bath
formulations.composition_detail: Ink: 4 wt% GelMA, 1 wt% gelatin, 0.5 wt% alginate. Support bath: 5 wt% GelMA with 11 mM CaCl2
formulations.cell_type: neural spheroids with astrocytes in the bath
formulations.key_outcome: Embedded printing in a brain-soft GelMA bath allowed patterned neurospheroid/astrocyte co-cultures.

evidence.quote: The bioink was prepared using 4 wt% GelMA, 1 wt% gelatin, 0.5 wt% alginate, and 0.25% PI dissolved in 40% HBSS, 60% MEM
The bioink was loaded into 1 ml syringes (BD) capped with 30 G needles (blunt, BD) and mounted on the extruder of a Cellink Inkredible bioprinter.
suspending astrocytes at a concentration of 8 × 106 cells ml−1 in a DMEM-based solution containing calcium chloride (CaCl2, 11 mM), PI (0.25 wt%), and freeze dried GelMA (5 wt%)
The compressive modulus of the 5 wt% GelMA hydrogels post UV exposure was measured to be 0.7 ± 0.1 kPa
